samples.question: The picture has two rows of cream panels. In the top row, the leftmost panel shows a token: a single coloured shape. Every other panel of the top row is a machine card, and the cards act on the token one at a time in order from left to right, as the arrow under the row shows. A card holding a grey shape sets the token's shape to that shape and leaves the token's colour unchanged. A card holding a wide, flat coloured bar sets the token's colour to that colour and leaves the token's shape unchanged. A later card of the same kind overwrites an earlier one, and a register that no card ever writes keeps the value drawn in the leftmost panel. The bottom row has four panels, numbered one to four from left to right, each holding one coloured shape. Exactly one of those four objects has both the shape and the colour that the token has after every card has acted. The token's final state is not drawn anywhere in the top row. Which of the four bottom panels holds that object? Answer with one word: one, two, three or four.
